messages:
Maya: Noticing two OOMs on p4d last night during the multi-tenant sweep. Symptoms look like sudden workspace expansion + large pref-cache shards.
Frank: Do you have which model / load shape? Any traces?
Maya: redwood-chat-16k-v1 (inference build). Mix of short (~8-64) and a few 1024 tails. The OOMs happened when many small requests overlapped with one large batch spike.
Ben: Pulled allocator stats from the window:
```
GPU total: 512GB
committed: 504GB
free: 8GB
external_frag: 15.1%
largest_free: 28MB
workspace_pool.current: 7.1GB
workspace_pool.peak: 12.2GB
size_class_counts: 64->1200, 128->560, 256->310
```
Sasha: Recent batching change (commit 9f3a2d) forces fused_attention for small batches which preallocates concat+temp buffers. That increases the workspace reservation per small batch.
Carla: TL;DR: allocator fragmentation + workspace growth + prefix cache holding a few large KV shards = cliff. Short fixes: reduce TTL for low-hit shards, cap small-batch workspace, and enable buffer reuse.
Maya: Can we quantify the TTL -> 300/600 tradeoffs? Need numbers before flipping in prod.
Ben: Ran a 24h replay with live traces: reducing default shard_ttl 3600->600 reduces pref-cache memory by ~18% median, but shard hit-rate drops 3.5% overall. Token-side latency increases ~5% p95 for affected requests due to reloads. I/O CPU cost up marginally.
Frank: 3.5% hit loss is acceptable if it stabilizes memory. We should mitigate tail latency by prefetching hottest prefixes for top customers.
Sasha: Also propose kernel-selection heuristic: for seq_len <=128 prefer compact-kernel which uses ~60% smaller workspace but ~+1% FLOPs (throughput hit minimal on large batches). That should avoid big temp allocations for small-batch-heavy traffic.
Carla: Short-term flip config we can canary:
```
prefix_cache:
  shard_ttl_default: 3600
  shard_ttl_low_hit: 600
  prefetch_hot_top_n: 10
workspace:
  small_batch_max_mb: 48   # was 128
  enable_buffer_reuse: true
kernel_selection:
  seq_len_threshold: 128
  low_ws_kernel: compact-kernel
```
Maya: Good. Add a canary plan and telemetry targets. Frank, can you run the canary to ~5% first and monitor OOM count, external_frag_pct, and p95 latency?
Frank: Yep. Canary plan: 5% traffic for 6h -> evaluate, then 25% for 12h if stable. Will alert if OOMs occur or p95 > baseline * 1.10.
Ben: I'll add allocator queries: external_frag_pct, num_large_fragments>32MB, avg_largest_free, reclaimed_buffers. Also add a defrag counter we'll increment when background coalesce runs.
Carla: Mid-term: switch to segregated freelists + on-demand coalescing when low util. In sims that halved external_frag_pct and reduced worst-case largest_free by ~60%.
Sasha: I'll prepare a microbenchmark for workspace allocation churn to validate compact-kernel + buffer reuse. Also a quick revert PR for the batching heuristic in case the canary regresses throughput badly.
DeployBot: alert: OOM on p4d-07 at 2026-02-12T03:21:14Z, instance drained (incident id 1829004321). Notified owners.
Maya: I'll open the incident doc, assign owners for canary rollout and telemetry. Ping me if you need extra repro nodes. :thumbsup:
